subject: chemistry
title: The carbon cycle and the greenhouse effect

scenes.heading: The carbon cycle and the greenhouse effect
scenes.sub: Every carbon atom in you was once part of the air
scenes.say: Every carbon atom in your body was once part of the air. Let's follow carbon around the Earth, and see how it controls how warm our planet is.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.science: Carbon moving between stores through flows
scenes.breaks: People choose to move money; carbon moves through natural processes, and no 'interest' is ever added.
scenes.say: Think of carbon as money moving between bank accounts. The accounts are carbon stores: the air, living things, oceans and rocks. The transfers are flows, like photosynthesis and burning. Fossil fuels are a term deposit, locked away for millions of years. Burning them withdraws it all at once.

scenes.heading: Mirror images

right.title: Respiration
points: All the time, day and night

scenes.say: Photosynthesis and respiration are mirror images. Photosynthesis is like charging a phone: plants use light to turn carbon dioxide and water into glucose, storing energy. Respiration is like using the phone: glucose reacts with oxygen, releasing energy and carbon dioxide. Plants respire all the time.

scenes.heading: Photosynthesis
scenes.say: Here's photosynthesis. Six carbon dioxide plus six water gives glucose plus six oxygen. Flip the arrow, and you've got respiration.

scenes.heading: The greenhouse effect
steps: Greenhouse gases send some back down
scenes.say: The greenhouse effect works in four steps. Sunlight passes through the air and warms the surface. The surface gives off infrared radiation. Greenhouse gases absorb some of it and re-emit it in all directions, including back down.

scenes.heading: Earth's doona
scenes.everyday: A doona slows down heat leaving your body
scenes.science: Greenhouse gases slow heat loss to space
scenes.breaks: A doona traps still air; greenhouse gases absorb and re-emit infrared – a different way of slowing heat loss.
scenes.say: It's like a doona: it doesn't make heat, it slows down heat loss. Without it, Earth would be roughly minus eighteen degrees instead of roughly fifteen. Natural is needed. The enhanced greenhouse effect is like adding an extra doona.
scenes.caption: It's like a doona: it doesn't make heat, it slows down heat loss. Without it, Earth would be roughly −18 °C instead of roughly 15 °C. Natural is needed. The enhanced greenhouse effect is like adding an extra doona.

scenes.heading: The enhanced greenhouse effect
points: Clearing forests: more CO₂, fewer plants
N₂ and O₂ are NOT greenhouse gases
scenes.say: Humans add greenhouse gases by burning fossil fuels, clearing forests, and farming livestock and rice, which release methane. Carbon dioxide has risen from roughly two hundred and eighty parts per million to over four hundred. That's causing global warming.
scenes.caption: Humans add greenhouse gases by burning fossil fuels, clearing forests, and farming livestock and rice, which release methane. CO₂ has risen from roughly 280 ppm to over 400 ppm. That's causing global warming.

points: Carbon moves between stores via flows
Natural is needed; enhanced is the problem
scenes.say: Quick recap. Carbon moves between stores. Photosynthesis removes carbon dioxide, while respiration and burning release it. Greenhouse gases keep Earth warm, but adding more is warming the planet. Now try the practice questions!
